description.en-US: The combo parent line this component belongs to. Immutable: moving a component between lines would change what two combos contained at once, and the line it left would keep an allocated amount it can no longer account for.

Position within the combo, unique per parent line. It is a stable identifier rather than display order: the allocation residual is assigned by a rule that breaks ties on it (D-04), so renumbering components would move sub-unit amounts between them and change what each one is recorded as having cost.

The real variant this component is. Required, unlike on the parent line: the whole reason components exist is that Inventory fulfils real variants and never a virtual combo (BR 17), so a component without one would be unfulfillable. A plain ulid, since the product belongs to Inventory.

The component product's code as it was when the sale happened. Snapshotted for the same reason as on the parent line: a product recoded next year must not change what a receipt issued today says was inside the bundle.
The component product's name as it appeared at the time of sale. This is what a customer sees itemised under the combo on their receipt.

How much of this variant the combo contains, in uom_id, for the parent line's whole ordered quantity. Must be strictly greater than zero, enforced by the domain service since the framework declares no CHECK constraints. Scale 6 matches the parent line: a component can legitimately be a fraction of a unit.

The unit this component's quantity is expressed in. It need not match the parent line's unit: a combo priced per box can contain a component measured in litres. Sales registers a UomUsageProbe covering this field, so Essential refuses to change a unit that sales history depends on.

This component's share of the parent line's net amount, allocated by the pricing engine (BR 18). The sum across a line's components must equal that line's net_amount EXACTLY: a bundle priced at one number has to be attributable back to its parts without gaining or losing a unit, or the fiscal document and the stock valuation disagree. D-04 fixes the residual rule that makes the sum exact.

This component's share of the parent line's tax. Taken from Accounting when it taxed the components individually, and otherwise allocated across them in proportion to their allocated net - the allocator guarantees the shares sum to the line's tax exactly, so a VAT invoice itemising a combo still adds up to what was charged.
